items.title: Model layer: primary pane flag in the split-tree model — default assignment to a group's first pane, per-group uniqueness, nearest-leaf promotion when the primary closes, persistence through the pane-layout path with restore normalization of 0/multiple primaries to exactly 1, and the overall-view display-target judgment — covered by XGhosttyTests

evidence.summary: Primary-pane model layer (SPEC §22 to be written in T-016). GroupState gains primaryPane (private(set) SurfaceID?, exactly one per non-empty tree by construction): init/decode normalize via SplitTree.normalizedPrimary (first stored valid flag wins, else first leaf — the 0/dangling/multiple repair), a paneTree didSet observer reconciles on every tree replacement via SplitTree.reconciledPrimary (later splits never take the flag; a departed primary promotes its nearest surviving leaf measured on the previous tree — shell exit / Cmd+W / process death all reach the model as such a replacement), setPrimaryPane rejects panes outside the tree and demotes the former primary implicitly, and the save format is a primaryPanes id-list riding the same GroupState record as the pane layout so a corrupt save can hold 0/dangling/several flags and decode repairs it. WorkspaceState gains overallViewPaneIDs ([GroupID: SurfaceID], visible groups -> their primary — the overall-view display-target judgment), forwarded by WorkspaceModel with primaryPaneID(of:). Testability refactor per Essence 思想 4: GroupState/WorkspaceState/WorkspaceModel became generic GroupStateOf/WorkspaceStateOf/WorkspaceModelOf over the pane element (runtime typealiases keep every call site unchanged; static stored properties became computed; WorkspaceError/CloseGroupOutcome moved to top-level non-generic enums WorkspaceModelError/WorkspaceCloseGroupOutcome with aliases, since Sendable synthesis inside the generic class would demand Pane: Sendable), so XGhosttyTests exercises the identical model code with value-type panes — real leaves in the trees, which SurfaceView construction (needs a live app) never allowed.

xcodebuild XGhosttyTests: TEST SUCCEEDED, 453 test cases, 0 failures — the full prior suite plus 18 new GroupPrimaryPaneTests: initial pane primary on new group and on WorkspaceModel(wrapping:), empty tree has none, later splits non-primary with the flag staying put, setPrimaryPane moves/demotes and rejects outside panes, nearest-leaf promotion on primary close ([A|B] and [A|[B|C]] rows), non-primary close keeps the flag, last-pane close clears it, GroupState Codable round trip keeps a non-default primary on the same pane, decode normalizes zero/missing-key/multiple/dangling primaryPanes to exactly one, whole-workspace round trip restores every group's primary, overall-view display set == each visible group's primary only (hidden excluded), and the controller-mirror path (replaceFocusedPaneTree) keeps/promotes the flag.

items.title: Overall view behavior: render only each group's primary pane (zoomed local view unchanged), direct keyboard input/focus to the primary, snap focus to the primary on zoom release, and no-op guards for pane operations (split, inter-pane focus movement, pane zoom, resize/equalize) outside zoom; guards covered by XGhosttyTests

evidence.summary: Overall-view behavior (SPEC §22.3-22.5, to be written in T-016). Model layer: WorkspaceState.paneOperationsEnabled (true only while zoomedGroup != nil && zoomedGroup == focusedGroup) and mutating snapFocusToPrimaryInOverallView() (outside zoom the focused group's focusedSurface snaps to its primary), called from every mutation that can land un-zoomed: replaceFocusedPaneTree (covers primary shell-exit promotion), setFocusedSurface, switchFocusedGroup, gotoGroup, toggleGroupZoom (the zoom-release snap), hideFocusedGroup, showGroup, closeFocusedGroup. GroupState.overallViewPaneTree derives the single-primary-leaf display tree. Rendering: TerminalWorkspaceView passes primaryOnly (zoomedGroup == nil) through GroupSplitTreeView/GroupSplitSubtreeView to GroupView, which renders overallViewPaneTree outside zoom and the full paneTree while zoomed. No-op guards: BaseTerminalController.newSplit, performSplitAction (divider resize + drop), ghosttyDidFocusSplit/ghosttyDidToggleSplitZoom/ghosttyDidResizeSplit/ghosttyDidEqualizeSplits all guard on workspace.paneOperationsEnabled; XGhostty.App performability checks (newSplit, gotoSplit, resizeSplit, toggleSplitZoom, equalizeSplits) decline before posting so performable keybinds fall through unconsumed; validateMenuItem grays out the 16 pane-op menu selectors. Focus wiring: ghosttyDidToggleGroupZoom targets the primary on release, ghosttyDidPresentTerminal and replaceSurfaceTree retarget focus to the primary while un-zoomed. Design judgment (recorded as R-005): canToggleGroupZoom now requires only a focused group — with pane ops zoom-only, a single-group workspace would otherwise never reach a split; zoom is the gateway to the local view.

evidence.summary: Pane-count badge (SPEC section 22.7, new; test inventory moved to 22.8). items.title: Unconditional group-close confirmation: close_group and last-pane Cmd+W always show the Cancel / Close Group dialog regardless of running processes, with XGhosttyTests covering the always-confirm requirement

evidence.summary: Always-confirm group close (SPEC section 23.1 to be written in T-028; authored in run R-20260810T160205+0900-7b3f90 / commit 9f707d8, reviewed and verified this cycle). The judgment lives on the model so tests can pin it: WorkspaceModel.closeGroupRequiresConfirmation(anyLiveProcess:) returns true unconditionally - the confirmed close-group dialog is the single sanctioned path that loses a group and its information. BaseTerminalController.closeFocusedGroup now consults that judgment instead of the surfaceTree needsConfirmQuit scan, so the existing Cancel / Close Group dialog appears regardless of running processes; ghosttyDidCloseSurface's last-pane escalation drops its groups.count>1 gate, so a single-group last-pane Cmd+W also escalates to the confirmed close_group (whose confirmed path still delegates to window close per section 18.5). Made sound by T-021: the core no longer closes surfaces on child exit, so every close_surface notification reaching the escalation is an explicit user operation - the always-confirm can never fire on a shell death.

items.title: Terminated-state model layer: last-pane shell exit (normal/abnormal/process death) keeps the group with its note as a terminated pane instead of closing; a single pane's exit in a multi-pane group still closes only that pane; terminated groups persist and restore with their notes; the primary-close last-pane path follows the terminated-state semantics; judgment logic in the model layer covered by XGhosttyTests

evidence.summary: Terminated-state model layer (SPEC section 23.2/23.4 to be written in T-028; authored in run R-20260810T160205+0900-7b3f90, committed as 9f707d8 when that session died with claude_exit_1 before verifying; reviewed and verified this cycle). Zig core: Surface.childExited no longer closes the surface (message trimmed to 'Process exited.'; the wait_after_command early-return removed - the app layer owns what an exit means), and keyCallback swallows encoded key input on an exited pane instead of closing, so every remaining core-initiated close is an explicit operation. App layer: show_child_exited posts the new ghosttyChildExited notification unconditionally (even window-less/hidden or instantly-exited panes) with an abnormal-exit Bool derived from abnormalCommandExitRuntime; the message-bar display keeps the upstream visibility guards. Model judgment (pure, value-type-testable): WorkspaceModel.childExitOutcome(for:abnormalExit:) - a group's last pane -> .terminated on every exit kind (normal/abnormal/process death arrive identically), a sibling pane -> .closePane (normal) / .keepPaneAwaitingKey (abnormal, upstream contract kept); GroupState.terminatedPane (private(set), invariant: non-nil only while that pane is the tree's sole leaf, cleared by the paneTree observer on splits/removals), markPaneTerminated (sole-leaf-only), removeExitedPane (model-side sibling close incl. hidden groups; rejects a last pane - that case is .terminated, never a removal), and a terminated primary keeps its flag (the primary-close last-pane path follows the terminated semantics, S-024). Persistence: the terminated state is runtime-only - a restore recreates every pane with a fresh shell so the group comes back live, while the note rides the existing GroupState record; loss paths unchanged (explicit confirmed close only, S-048). Controller: ghosttyDidExitChild routes the outcome (mark terminated / close the exited pane via the focused-tree path or model-side removal / keep awaiting key).

Targeted run this cycle: TEST SUCCEEDED, all 16 GroupTerminatedTests named passing in the log, covering every S-050 model criterion: last-pane exit judged .terminated for every exit kind; markPaneTerminated keeps the group with its note and pane (and rejects a pane among several); sibling normal exit judged .closePane and removeExitedPane closes only that pane (note kept, hidden-group path included; a group's last pane rejected); terminated-group Codable round trip keeps the note (the state itself is runtime-only, so the group restores live); a terminated primary last pane keeps its flag; the outcome is re-judged after siblings close (promotes to .terminated); splitting while terminated clears the state; restart transition covered (fresh pane in the same slot / rejected when not terminated).

items.title: Terminated pane UI and restart: a terminated pane renders a terminal-fitting terminated view, and pressing Enter starts a new shell in the same pane to resume work

evidence.summary: Terminated pane UI and Enter restart (SPEC section 23.3 to be written in T-028; authored in run R-20260810T160205+0900-7b3f90 / commit 9f707d8, reviewed and verified this cycle). UI: new GroupTerminatedPaneView rendered by GroupView over the pane area while the group is terminated - the dead terminal's last frame stays visible but dimmed (the final output often says how the shell ended), with a terminal-styled panel (poweroff glyph, 'Shell exited', 'Press Return to start a new shell' hint, monospaced type, the terminal's own background color and split-divider stroke - the note-surface styling family); hit-testing disabled so clicking a terminated group still focuses it, which routes the subsequent Enter to the restart path. Key routing: SurfaceView.keyDown posts ghosttyExitedSurfaceKeyDown (with an isReturn flag) for exited panes instead of writing to the dead pty - only plain keyDowns land there, so command chords (Cmd+W etc.) keep working on an exited pane. Controller: on Enter for a terminated group, restartTerminatedPane builds a fresh SurfaceView (fresh shell), swaps it into the same pane slot via the model (WorkspaceModel.restartTerminatedPane: the new pane becomes primary and the focused surface, note kept), re-syncs surfaceTree and moves keyboard focus when the group is focused; a non-terminated exited pane keeps the upstream any-key-closes contract, re-judged at key time so a pane whose siblings have since closed terminates instead of closing.

Targeted run this cycle: TEST SUCCEEDED - the restart transition's model semantics pass: restartTerminatedPaneStartsFreshPaneInSameSlot (fresh pane in the same sole slot, becomes primary and focused surface, note kept, terminated state cleared) and restartIsRejectedWhenNotTerminated, plus exitOutcomeIsRejudgedAfterSiblingsClosed for the key-time re-judgment.
Success-criterion 3 gate this cycle: full XGhosttyTests suite TEST SUCCEEDED (exit 0) with the terminated cover view and the exited-pane key routing in the tree.

items.title: Note editor standard text-editing shortcuts: Cmd+A / Cmd+C / Cmd+X / Cmd+V act on the editor while the note edit overlay is shown; pastes that push the note over 10 lines truncate to the first 10 on save (existing cap unchanged)

evidence.summary: Standard text-editing chords in the note editor (SPEC §21.2). Cause: the Edit menu's key equivalents are synced from config to terminal actions (copy_to_clipboard / paste_from_clipboard / select_all, AppDelegate.syncMenuShortcuts), so Cmd+A/C/X/V matched menu items that never reach the overlay's text view. Fix: four hidden keyboardShortcut receivers inside the GroupNoteEditor ZStack (the proven Cmd+Enter hidden-button pattern) forward Cmd+A/C/X/V to the first responder — the focused editor text view — as the standard selectAll:/copy:/cut:/paste: selectors via NSApp.sendAction(to: nil). The window hierarchy's key-equivalent pass runs before the menu bar's, so the forwarding wins only while the overlay exists; terminal copy/paste outside the editor is unchanged (S-010 sanctioned exception). Paste truncation (S-037) needed no code change: the existing save path normalizes CRLF/CR to LF and caps at maxNoteLines (GroupState.normalizedNote), now locked in by the new test endNoteEditingTruncatesOversizedPasteToFirstTenLines (14 CRLF-separated pasted lines -> exactly the first 10 lines stored). SPEC.md §21.2 documents the chord routing and the paste cap; §21.4 test inventory extended.
